fixtures.title: Improper integral: width and limit steps
fixtures.text:
The integral is improper because the denominator is zero at \(x=3\).

| steps in math | steps in words |
| --- | --- |
| \int_3^4\frac{x}{x^2-9}\,dx=\lim_{a\to3^+}\int_a^4\frac{x}{x^2-9}\,dx | Approach the lower endpoint from the right. |
| u=x^2-9 | Use this substitution. |
| du=2x\,dx\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x\,dx=\frac{du}{2} | Differentiate, then isolate x dx. |
| \int_3^4\frac{x}{x^2-9}\,dx=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0^+}\frac{1}{2}\int_{\varepsilon}^7\frac{du}{u} | The bounds become 0 and 7. Keep the lower endpoint as a limit. |
| \lim_{\varepsilon\to0^+}\frac{1}{2}\left[\log u\right]_{\varepsilon}^7=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0^+}\frac{1}{2}\left(\log7-\log\varepsilon\right)=+\infty | As epsilon tends to zero from above, log epsilon tends to negative infinity; subtracting it makes the result tend to positive infinity. |
| \boxed{\text{Final: the integral diverges to positive infinity.}} | The improper integral has no finite value. |
